open_obligations.what_is_open: On the explicitly balanced exhaustive domain \(K\mid N\), construct a recognition algorithm polynomial in \(N\), \(K\), and the rational input bit length for membership of \([\Omega]_{\cong}\) in \(\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\), returning a common relabelling and a finite cut certificate on yes instances and an arm-specific binary ordered-column witness with a strict exact loss improvement on no instances; alternatively, prove a complexity obstruction that remains valid after restricting \(\Omega\) to the admissible moment-polytope image \(\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\). If binary separation is incomplete on that image, determine the least uniform finite alphabet size that is complete.
open_obligations.obstruction: The finite copositivity characterization reduces a fixed relabelling \(\pi\) to copositivity of one explicit matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\) for every arm-permutation tuple \(\sigma\). Its exact algorithm enumerates \(N!\) common relabellings, \((N!)^K\) arm-permutation tuples, all nonempty principal supports in dimension \(K(N-1)\), and the negative eigenspaces of the resulting principal matrices. This proves termination but no polynomial bound. Moreover, a negative vector in \(\mathbb R_+^{K(N-1)}\) can have several positive adjacent increments in one arm, whereas a binary ordered column has at most one positive adjacent increment. Thus the proved copositivity witness cannot in general be converted to a binary witness by the available argument. The frozen primitives contain neither a structural theorem for matrices arising from admissible balanced covariance moments nor a faithful reduction showing that the unrestricted difficulty survives that moment-polytope restriction.
open_obligations.attempted: Use the unique suffix-cut expansion of every monotone arm column, cancel constant terms by the balanced kernel row- and column-sum identities, and express every identity-versus-permutation loss difference as \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}B^{\pi,\sigma}\alpha\) with \(\alpha\geq0\). Then characterize noncopositivity by a nonempty principal support whose principal matrix has a negative eigenvalue with a strictly positive eigenvector, and decide the resulting tests by exact real-algebraic root isolation and ordered-field linear feasibility. This yields the exact exhaustive algorithm and multilevel witnesses. Restricting to a single suffix cut per arm was also tested, but it examines only a strict subset of the nonnegative increment cone and does not control mixed cut-product terms. No admissibility identity presently forces a negative quadratic form to attain negativity on that subset.
open_obligations.partial_result: For every rational \(H\in\mathbb S_+^K\) and rational admissible \(\Omega\in\mathfrak K^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\) on the domain \(K\mid N\), orbit membership is decidable exactly: \([\Omega]_{\cong}\in\mathfrak C^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}(H)\) if and only if there exists \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_N\) for which every explicit cut matrix \(B^{\pi,\sigma}\), \(\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N^K\), is copositive. For a symmetric matrix \(B\), copositivity is equivalent to the absence, for every nonempty principal support \(I\) and negative eigenvalue \(\lambda<0\) of \(B[I]\), of a vector in \(\ker\{B[I]-\lambda I_I\}\cap\mathbb R_{++}^I\). Exact root isolation and ordered-field feasibility therefore terminate. On failure, a positive eigenvector produces ordered columns \(x_i^a=\sum_{r<i}\alpha_{ar}\) with at most \(N\) levels and satisfies \[\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\mathrm{id})-\mathscr L_{H,\Omega^\pi}(x,\sigma)=\lambda\lVert\alpha\rVert_2^2<0.\] This is a complete exact multilevel certificate, but the enumeration is not polynomial and the bound of \(N\) levels is only an upper bound, not a proof of the least complete alphabet.
